Mehmet Oz, MD, MBA 
Administrator 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services

Thomas Keane, MD, MBA

Washington, DC 20201 
 
Submitted electronically via www.regulations.gov 
 
Re: Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs Proposed Rule 
 
Dear Administrator Oz and National Coordinator Keane: 
 
On behalf of the Obesity Medicine Association (OMA), we appreciate the opportunity to provide feedback on 
the aforementioned proposed rule. The OMA is the largest organization of physicians, nurse practitioners, 
physician assistants, and other health care providers who work to improve the lives of patients affected by 
obesity. OMA members are clinical experts in obesity medicine. They use a comprehensive, scientific, and 
individualized approach when treating obesity, which helps patients achieve their health and weight goals.  
Interoperability Standards for APIs 
OMA supports CMSâ€™ proposals to require impacted payers to implement and maintain Application 
Programming Interface (API) technology that conforms with updated interoperability standards adopted by the 
Secretary in regulation, as well as CMSâ€™ proposals related to standards for electronic prior authorization of 
drugs covered under a pharmacy benefit, including use of the NCPDP SCRIPT standard and related 
implementation specifications. OMA agrees that establishing clear, standardized interoperability and electronic 
prior authorization requirements for impacted payers is important to promoting more consistent electronic 
exchange of prior authorization, formulary, and utilization management information across plans and systems 
and reducing administrative burden associated with varying payer requirements and workflows. 
Electronic Prior Authorization for Drugs 
OMA supports CMSâ€™ proposal to require state Medicaid and CHIP fee-for-service programs, Medicaid 
managed care plans, CHIP managed care entities, and Qualified Health Plan (QHP) issuers on the Federally 
Facilitated Exchanges (FFEs) to support an unexpired version of the NCPDP SCRIPT standard adopted by 
the Secretary for electronic prior authorization of drugs covered under a pharmacy benefit. OMA also supports 
CMSâ€™ proposals requiring support for the NCPDP Formulary and Benefit (F&B) standard and the NCPDP 
Real-Time Prescription Benefit (RTPB) standard. OMA agrees that aligning electronic prior authorization and 
related pharmacy benefit standards across impacted payers, Medicare Part D sponsors, prescribers, 
dispensers, and other federal interoperability initiatives can help promote more standardized prior 
authorization workflows, improve transparency regarding coverage and utilization management requirements, 
and reduce administrative burden associated with inconsistent payer requirements and processes for 
prescription drugs. 
Improving Communications and Decision Timeframes for Prior Authorizations 
 
Proposed Requirement to Include a Specific Reason for Denial in Response to Prior Authorization Requests 
for All Drugs 
OMA supports CMSâ€™ proposal to require state Medicaid and CHIP fee-for-service programs, Medicaid 
managed care plans, CHIP managed care entities, and QHP issuers on the FFEs to provide providers with a 
specific reason for denial of prior authorization requests for drugs, regardless of the method used to send the 
prior authorization request or decision. OMA appreciates CMSâ€™ efforts to expand these transparency 
requirements across additional impacted payers, which could help physicians better understand utilization 
management requirements, more efficiently address coverage barriers, and facilitate resubmissions or 
appeals when medically necessary obesity medications are denied. More detailed denial communications will 
be particularly important for obesity medications, where physicians and patients frequently encounter changing 
coverage criteria, repeated documentation requirements, and step therapy barriers across impacted payers. 
 
 
 
Prior Authorization Decision Timeframes 
OMA appreciates CMSâ€™ proposals to establish more consistent and expedited prior authorization decision 
timeframes for prescription drugs across impacted payers, building on existing decision timeframe 
requirements that already apply to certain drugs under Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and CHIP programs. 
While we appreciate CMSâ€™ proposals, we are concerned about the lack of alignment across impacted payers 
and we urge CMS to use rulemaking to continue pursuing alignment toward a 24-hour maximum response 
timeframe for prescription drug prior authorization requests across impacted payers, including Medicare 
Advantage. More consistent and expedited prior authorization decision timeframes could help reduce 
treatment delays, minimize disruptions in continuity of care, and improve patient access to medically 
necessary obesity medications and other chronic disease therapies.  
 
Proposed Requirement to Publicly Report Prior Authorization Metrics for Drugs for Impacted Payers 
OMA supports CMSâ€™ proposals requiring impacted payers to publicly report prior authorization metrics related 
to prescription drugs. We agree that increased transparency regarding prior authorization approval rates, 
denial rates, appeals, and review timeframes could provide important insight into how utilization management 
policies affect patient access to medications. OMA urges CMS to require impacted payers to provide more 
detailed and drug-specific reporting for therapeutic categories that are frequently subject to intensive utilization 
management requirements, including obesity medications. More granular reporting could be particularly 
valuable in identifying patterns of excessive denials, repeated prior authorization requirements, delays 
associated with step therapy protocols, and other barriers that may disrupt continuity of care and timely access 
to clinically appropriate treatment.  
These transparency efforts may become increasingly important as utilization management approaches 
continue to evolve across impacted payers and newer care delivery and payment models, particularly for 
obesity medicines, potentially resulting in varying prior authorization and step therapy requirements that affect 
continuity of care and treatment access. 
Updates to Patient Access, Provider Directory, Provider Access, and Payer-to-Payer APIs; API Usage 
Metrics 
OMA supports proposals requiring impacted payers to add information about prior authorization requests and 
decisions for drugs to the Patient Access, Provider Access, and Payer-to-Payer APIs. OMA also encourages 
CMS to ensure these efforts include step therapy requirements and related utilization management information 
to support continuity of care when patients transition between payers. For obesity medications, timely access 
to prior authorization status, coverage determinations, and utilization management requirements may be 
particularly important given the frequency of changing coverage criteria, step therapy protocols, and 
documentation requirements across impacted payers and pharmacy benefit structures. 
 
OMA is also concerned about the proposal to remove formulary information from the Provider Access and 
Payer-to-Payer APIs. We disagree that providers have sufficient access to formulary and utilization 
management information through existing payer websites and standard communications materials, particularly 
given the frequency with which coverage criteria, preferred product status, prior authorization requirements, 
and related utilization management policies may change across impacted payers. Physicians treating obesity 
frequently must review and compare varying formulary and coverage requirements across plans to support 
continuity of treatment and help patients maintain access to clinically appropriate therapies. OMA believes that 
retaining formulary information within these APIs could help support more efficient access to coverage and 
utilization management information, reduce fragmented workflows associated with coverage verification and 
prior authorization processes, and improve continuity of care when patients transition between plans or 
coverage arrangements. 
Requests for Information: Step Therapy 
OMA appreciates CMSâ€™ focus on improving step therapy processes through interoperability and data sharing. 
Obesity is a chronic disease that requires long-term treatment continuity and medication management which is 
individualized to each patient. Patientsâ€™ response and tolerability to obesity medications can vary significantly, 
making continuity of clinically effective therapy imperative for optimal patient outcomes. 
 
Unfortunately, patients receiving obesity treatment frequently experience disruptions in care when transitioning 
between payers or when prior treatment history is not readily accessible to the new plan. Repeated or 
duplicative step therapy requirements, changing formulary requirements, and interruptions associated with 
payer transitions can disrupt clinically effective treatment and create unnecessary administrative burden for 
physician practices and patients. Clinicians treating obesity also increasingly encounter repeated prior 
authorization submissions and varying documentation requirements for GLP-1 therapies across impacted 
payers, including requirements related to dose escalation, continuation of therapy, prior treatment attempts, 
and lifestyle program participation. In some cases, patients who are clinically stable on a therapy may 
experience treatment interruptions or be required to switch medications due to formulary or utilization 
management changes. 
 
 
 
OMA encourages CMS and ONC to work with stakeholders to develop interoperability tools and data 
exchange capabilities that support continuity of care and recognition of prior payer determinations, step 
therapy history, and related utilization management information across impacted payers. OMA also 
encourages CMS to explore how interoperability and data-sharing tools could help minimize duplicative step 
therapy requirements and support more consistent utilization management processes for obesity medications 
across impacted payers and coverage models. 
Other Challenges: Emerging Obesity Medication Coverage and Utilization Management Models 
OMA requests additional clarification regarding how prior authorization, interoperability, and related utilization 
management requirements will apply within newer coverage and payment approaches for obesity medications, 
including the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Model and the Better Approaches to Lifestyle and Nutrition for 
Comprehensive hEalth (BALANCE) Model. For example, will the central processor under the Medicare GLP-1 
Bridge Model or Part D plans under BALANCE be required to utilize the proposed APIs and NCPDP SCRIPT 
standards to process prior authorization requests, to respond to prior authorization requests within 72 hours, 
and provide denial reasons for GLP-1 drugs covered under the models? Likewise, will these entities be 
required to publicly report data on prior authorization requests on an annual basis, consistent with proposals in 
this rule? OMA encourages CMS to ensure that policies are applied consistently across these models and 
participating entities to avoid creating additional fragmentation and administrative burden for physician 
practices and beneficiaries. 
 
As CMS continues implementing these models and related utilization management requirements for obesity 
medications, OMA encourages CMS to prioritize alignment, transparency, and operational consistency across 
participating payers and entities. OMA also encourages CMS to ensure that electronic prior authorization, 
interoperability, and data-sharing initiatives support continuity of care and minimize duplicative utilization 
management requirements when patients transition between plans, programs, or coverage models.  
 
*** 
 
Thank you for opportunity to comment on the aforementioned proposed rule.  Please feel free to contact 
Carolynn Francavilla Brown, MD, DABOM, MFOMA, Vice President of the OMAâ€™s Board of Trustees at 
doctorfrancavilla@gmail.com, should you have any questions or need additional information.  
 
Sincerely, 
 
 
Teresa Fraker, FACHE, RN, CPHQ, CAE 
Executive Director 
Obesity Medicine Association 
7173 South Havana Street 
#600-130 
Centennial, CO 80112 
E-mail:  tfraker@obesitymedicine.org
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Obesity Medicine Association (OMA); signed by Teresa Fraker, FACHE, RN, CPHQ, CAE, Executive Director.
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** OMA represents physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and other clinicians specializing in obesity medicine.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

OMA generally supports CMS's interoperability and electronic drug prior authorization proposals, including NCPDP SCRIPT, Formulary & Benefit, and Real-Time Prescription Benefit requirements. It asks CMS to align drug PA timeframes toward a 24-hour maximum, require drug-specific and therapeutic-category reporting, retain formulary information in Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs, improve step therapy data exchange, and clarify how requirements apply to emerging obesity medication coverage models.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; PA-DENIAL-REASONS; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS; API-USAGE-METRICS; API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING; GENERAL.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** None specifically.
- **Standards referenced:** API technology; NCPDP SCRIPT; NCPDP Formulary & Benefit; NCPDP Real-Time Prescription Benefit; Patient Access API; Provider Access API; Payer-to-Payer API; Provider Directory API.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Interoperability API standards**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Standardized interoperability requirements promote consistent exchange of PA, formulary, and utilization-management information and reduce varying payer workflows.
- **Specific request:** Finalize clear standardized API requirements for impacted payers.

**Topic 2: Electronic PA for pharmacy benefit drugs**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Alignment across impacted payers, Part D sponsors, prescribers, dispensers, and federal initiatives can improve transparency and reduce inconsistent processes.
- **Specific request:** Require support for unexpired NCPDP SCRIPT, Formulary & Benefit, and RTPB standards.

**Topic 3: Specific denial reasons**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Detailed denial communications help physicians understand coverage barriers, resubmit, and appeal when obesity medications are denied.
- **Specific request:** Require specific denial reasons for all drug PA requests regardless of method.

**Topic 4: Decision timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Inconsistent timeframes across impacted payers can delay access and disrupt continuity of obesity and chronic disease treatment.
- **Specific request:** Continue rulemaking toward a 24-hour maximum prescription drug PA response timeframe across impacted payers, including Medicare Advantage.

**Topic 5: Public PA metrics**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Aggregate metrics may not reveal intensive utilization management affecting obesity medications.
- **Specific request:** Require detailed, drug-specific and therapeutic-category reporting for categories frequently subject to intensive UM, including obesity medications.

**Topic 6: Formulary information in APIs**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Oppose/Modify
- **Rationale:** Provider websites and standard communications are insufficient because coverage criteria and preferred product status change frequently.
- **Specific request:** Do not remove formulary information from Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs.

**Topic 7: Step therapy and payer transitions**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Duplicative step therapy, prior treatment history gaps, and formulary changes disrupt clinically effective obesity treatment.
- **Specific request:** Develop data exchange tools that recognize prior payer determinations, step therapy history, and UM information across impacted payers.

**Topic 8: Emerging obesity medication models**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Clarify
- **Rationale:** New models may create fragmentation if standards, timeframes, denial reasons, and reporting do not apply consistently.
- **Specific request:** Clarify applicability to the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Model, BALANCE Model, central processors, and Part D plans under those models.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S14:** OMA supports applying NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB pharmacy benefit standards across impacted payers.
- **S16:** OMA supports requiring specific denial reasons for drug PA requests.
- **S19/S22:** OMA supports cross-payer pharmacy standard alignment and sees it as burden-reducing, though it does not provide detailed state readiness or cost estimates.
- **S20/S43:** OMA urges alignment toward a 24-hour maximum response timeframe across impacted payers, including Medicare Advantage.
- **S29/S35:** OMA supports public reporting of drug PA metrics and requests more granular drug-specific and therapeutic-category data.
- **S66-S82:** OMA responds to step therapy and continuity-of-care RFIs by recommending exchange of prior payer determinations, step therapy history, and utilization-management information.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Finalize standardized API requirements for impacted payers.
2. Require support for unexpired NCPDP SCRIPT, Formulary & Benefit, and RTPB standards.
3. Require specific denial reasons for all drug PA denials.
4. Align prescription drug PA decision timeframes toward a 24-hour maximum across impacted payers.
5. Require drug-specific and therapeutic-category PA reporting, especially for obesity medications.
6. Retain formulary information in Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs.
7. Develop interoperability tools that preserve prior PA determinations, step therapy history, and UM information across payer transitions.
8. Clarify applicability of PA and interoperability requirements to Medicare GLP-1 Bridge and BALANCE model entities.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** Lack of payer alignment, removal of formulary data from APIs, duplicative step therapy, inconsistent obesity medication coverage criteria, and unclear treatment of emerging coverage/payment models.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Treatment delays, disrupted continuity of care, repeated documentation, therapy interruption, forced switching, and administrative burden for physician practices and patients.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Changing coverage criteria, variable documentation requirements, payer transitions, changing formularies, and fragmented models.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** None quantified.
- **Studies or research referenced:** None.
- **Examples provided:** GLP-1 therapies, dose escalation, continuation therapy, prior treatment attempts, lifestyle program participation, Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Model, BALANCE Model, obesity medications subject to step therapy and changing formularies.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Obesity medicine clinicians, patients with obesity, impacted payers, Part D sponsors, Medicaid/CHIP programs, QHP issuers, prescribers, dispensers, and model participants.
- **Economic implications:** Standardization may reduce administrative burden; inconsistent UM may increase costs through repeated submissions and disrupted care.
- **Technical feasibility:** OMA supports standardized NCPDP and API implementation, with added data exchange for step therapy and formulary information.
- **Patient care impact:** Strong focus on continuity of obesity medication therapy and avoiding delays or interruptions.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive with targeted modifications
- **Tone:** Professional, collaborative, clinically focused
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "OMA supports CMS's proposals... including use of the NCPDP SCRIPT standard and related implementation specifications." - Context: Supporting pharmacy benefit drug standards.
2. "We urge CMS to use rulemaking to continue pursuing alignment toward a 24-hour maximum response timeframe." - Context: Requesting tighter decision timeframe alignment.
3. "OMA is also concerned about the proposal to remove formulary information from the Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs." - Context: Opposing removal of formulary data.
4. "Repeated or duplicative step therapy requirements... can disrupt clinically effective treatment." - Context: Explaining step therapy concerns for obesity medicine.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - OMA requests alignment toward a 24-hour PA response timeframe.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - The comment focuses on repeated submissions, documentation, and fragmented workflows.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - It supports API and NCPDP standard implementation and asks for additional data exchange capabilities.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - It endorses NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB standards.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Continuity of obesity medication therapy is a central concern.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - OMA asks CMS and ONC to work with stakeholders and align models/entities.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - It supports denial reasons, reporting, and formulary/UM visibility.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - It addresses current payer websites, documentation practices, and payer-transition workflows.
